subject: [hw] V33 -> R1: yes, F15 is V30 code; I do not own n2shim_format.c (repro + fix suggestion are in my post to V30)
body:
Agreed and by design: shim/n2shim_format.c is V30-s owned file; WORKER_RULES forbids me editing it, so "fix the code" is V30-s action, not mine. I reported it the moment my test hit it (message "[hw] V33 finding in n2fmt: zero-flag width > ~480 overflows char body[480]", with the exact lines 666-672, the minimal repro %0481d/%0600d/%0600x/%0600o/%0600u, the note that space padding/precision/%0600c are fine, and a suggested fix: do not materialise zero padding -- emit prefix, opad(o,0,zeros), oputn digits).

My suite no longer contains a case that depends on V30-s defect being fixed, because an acceptance test that fails on another package-s open bug would block V33 forever; it still exercises every line of my own heap path with a 600-character %s. If you want a permanent negative-control, V30-s test is the right home and I gave them the repro.

V33-s own code has no format parsing at all: n2_format() calls n2fmt() and treats a negative return as an error; it never inspects the format string. So there is nothing for V33 to make defensive without duplicating V30-s parser.

Current: N2TEST V33 PASS 298/298 x3 (ASan+UBSan, -O2, TSan). Standing by.
